name: Boredoms
label: Warner Bros.
lede: The singer's other band drove an excavator through a club wall; Boredoms went from that to a Warner Bros. contract, the Lollapalooza main stage, and sunset drum rituals for 77, 88 and 111 players.

eras.title: Acid Makki & Combi and Zombie
eras.text: Before Boredoms, Yamantaka Eye fronted Hanatarash, an Osaka noise act that played with drills, saws and a machete, and, per Wikipedia, once drove an excavator through a venue's back wall onto the stage. Most clubs banned them. Boredoms started as the punk band next door and soon had its own bad reputation.

years.h: Boredoms form in Osaka as Acid Makki & Combi and Zombie
years.p: Yamantaka Eye starts a noise-punk band with Hanatarash drummer Ikuo Taketani, guitarist Tabata Mitsuru, bassist Hosoi Hisato and singer Makki Sasarato. Their first recording, U.S.A., goes on a compilation tape.

years.h: The band renames itself after a Buzzcocks song
years.p: Makki Sasarato leaves, Yoshikawa Toyohito takes the drums and Hira the bass, and the band becomes Boredoms, after the [[Buzzcocks|31e9c35b-2675-4632-8596-f9bd9286f6c8]] song Boredom.

years.h: Anal by Anal · the first Boredoms EP
years.p: Yamantaka Eye and Tabata Mitsuru cut Boredoms' first official release, a short EP whose title set the tone for the band's taste in names.

years.h: Tabata leaves for Zeni Geva; Seiichi Yamamoto joins
years.p: Guitarist Tabata Mitsuru quits Boredoms to join [[Zeni Geva|4a48f534-9b66-495c-a934-b775beda1ca7]]. [[Seiichi Yamamoto|d35596ac-7786-4f50-abb5-cc4fb501ccb7]] takes over on guitar.

years.h: Osorezan no Stooges Kyo · first album
years.p: Boredoms' first full-length: harsh, dissonant punk that Yamantaka Eye cut up and re-edited in the studio, with nods to [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] and [[Funkadelic|cf042013-3edd-46c4-9b0e-a62faac98d0b]].

years.h: Yoshimi P-We joins on drums, the first woman in Boredoms
years.p: Unhappy with Yoshikawa Toyohito's drumming, Boredoms bring in [[Yoshimi P-We|fa119f2e-f1a1-4f3a-bd12-900d43ba7ce3]] from Eye's side project UFO or Die. Yoshikawa moves to percussion, then leaves.

eras.title: A major label's strangest signing
eras.text: Boredoms got to America through Sonic Youth and John Zorn, and Warner Bros. signed them. What followed was some of the most unhinged music ever issued by a major, tours with Sonic Youth and Nirvana, and a slot on the Lollapalooza main stage.

years.h: Soul Discharge · the record that crossed the Pacific
years.p: Boredoms' second album gets a US release, and the band lands long-term deals with Warner in Japan and its Reprise imprint in America.

years.h: Yamantaka Eye sings for John Zorn's Naked City
years.p: Eye becomes a guest vocalist in [[John Zorn|7ec4a553-73e5-4c0d-a071-a82b83a309e6]]'s [[Naked City|fc4dea85-3998-4130-a56e-907689160480]] and befriends Sonic Youth. Wikipedia counts both among Boredoms' ties to New York's downtown scene.

years.h: ATR becomes the drummer after Chew Hasegawa's short stint
years.p: After Chew Hasegawa fills in briefly, Kazuya Nishimura, known as ATR, takes the second drum seat alongside Yoshimi P-We.

years.h: Pop Tatari · Warner's strangest release
years.p: Boredoms' first major-label album. Wikipedia notes it is widely called one of the strangest albums a major label ever put out. The band tours with Sonic Youth.

years.h: Yamantaka Eye and Sonic Youth make TV Shit
years.p: Eye records the TV Shit EP with [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] for [[Thurston Moore|8ba48525-d922-42ee-9775-97b7b8f9712e]]'s Ecstatic Peace label. With Zorn, as Mystic Fugu Orchestra, he makes the first release on Zorn's Tzadik.

years.h: Eight straight nights opening for Nirvana
years.p: From late October into early November 1993, Boredoms play eight consecutive shows supporting [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]]. They also tour with grindcore band [[Brutal Truth|4ddc0620-38e2-40ec-8915-009967520168]] that year.

years.h: Chocolate Synthesizer · Reprise
years.p: Boredoms' next Reprise album sold well for a band this experimental, per Wikipedia. Alternative Press later put it among the 90 greatest albums of the '90s.

years.h: Boredoms on the Lollapalooza main stage
years.p: At the height of their US profile, Boredoms play the main stage of the 1994 Lollapalooza tour, supporting the just-released Chocolate Synthesizer.

years.h: EDA joins, via Pavement's Mark Ibold; Reprise lets them go
years.p: Percussionist EDA joins after an introduction from [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]] bassist [[Mark Ibold|003db9eb-2a01-4ece-a5e0-87000aa502d7]]. The same year Reprise drops Boredoms from its roster.

eras.title: Into the sun, then gone
eras.text: The noise didn't stop, it turned into orbit. By the late '90s Boredoms were making long, drum-heavy psychedelic jams that critics tied to krautrock and Can, and Vision Creation Newsun is often called their peak. Then, after a remix album, they vanished for years.

years.h: Super æ · space-sludge
years.p: After the Super Go!!!!!! EP, Boredoms' Super æ trades Japanoise for long psychedelic jams. Pitchfork put it on its Top 100 Albums of the 1990s.

years.h: Vision Creation Newsun · the one fans call the peak
years.p: Tribal multi-drum grooves, cosmic synths and bursts of noise, released in Japan in 1999. Wikipedia says it's often considered the band's greatest achievement.

years.cap: Beck's Midnite Vultures (1999), art by Yamantaka Eye
years.h: Yamantaka Eye draws Beck's Midnite Vultures cover
years.p: Eye, who made the art for most Boredoms records, also did the covers for Beck's Midnite Vultures, the Sexx Laws single and the Stray Blues B-sides set.

years.h: Rebore, vol. 0, then silence
years.p: Eye oversees a series of guest-DJ remix albums of the Boredoms catalog, releasing his own, Rebore, vol. 0, in 2000. Then no records, no tours for years.

years.h: The Flaming Lips name an album after Yoshimi P-We
years.p: While Boredoms are dormant, [[The Flaming Lips|1f43d76f-8edf-44f6-aaf1-b65f05ad9402]] release Yoshimi Battles the Pink Robots. Yoshimi plays on it, and Wayne Coyne said she inspired it.

eras.title: V∞redoms
eras.text: The rumored breakup wasn't one. A slimmed-down lineup came back as V∞redoms, the infinity sign built into the name, with three drummers and a synthesizer. They left Warner for the small Japanese label Commmons and found Thrill Jockey for the rest of the world.

years.h: Boredoms return as V∞redoms
years.p: Eye, Yoshimi P-We, ATR, EDA and synth player Izumi Kiyoshi resurface as V∞redoms, a three-drummer lineup. The band signs with Vice Records in the US.

years.h: Seadrum/House of Sun · first album in four years
years.p: Mostly recorded before the hiatus, it moves Boredoms from WEA Japan to the small label Commmons. Reviews were mostly positive, 73 on Metacritic.

years.h: A Christmas Eve show becomes Super Roots 9
years.p: Boredoms' Christmas Eve 2004 concert is recorded; it comes out in 2007 as Super Roots 9, the first Super Roots release since 1999.

years.h: EDA leaves; Yojiro Tatekawa takes the drum seat
years.p: After Seadrum, EDA quits to start the audio-visual project Adrena Adrena with artist Daisy Dickinson. Yojiro Tatekawa replaces EDA; ATR is also gone.

years.h: Three shows in Japan with Sonic Youth
years.p: Billed as V∞redoms, the band plays three dates with [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] in Japan, Pitchfork reported.

years.h: 77 Boadrum: 77 drummers in Brooklyn at 7:07 pm
years.p: At 7:07 pm on 7/7/07, Boredoms lead 77 drummers at the Empire–Fulton Ferry section of Brooklyn Bridge Park. Yoshimi P-We is drummer one.
years.xp: Eye said the number came from climbing the Temple of the Sun at Palenque in Mexico and counting 77 steps. Drummer Muneomi Senju sat in with the band. The event became a template the band ran again in 2008, 2009 and 2011, each time on a matching date.

eras.title: Boadrum by the numbers
eras.text: Now on Thrill Jockey outside Japan, Boredoms turned the Boadrum into a traveling ritual: 88 drummers at the La Brea Tar Pits, nine at Terminal 5, 111 on a beach in Australia. Eye added a seven-necked guitar and motion sensors, and the band kept growing sideways.

years.h: Tiny Mix Tapes: Boredoms sign to Thrill Jockey
years.p: Tiny Mix Tapes breaks the Boredoms signing with a headline declaring Thrill Jockey is fucking awesome. The label handles the band outside Japan from here.

years.h: Eye's seven-necked guitar, on tour with Iron & Wine
years.p: On a 2008 US tour with [[Iron & Wine|c3f28da8-662d-4f09-bdc7-3084bf685930]], Yamantaka Eye plays a new seven-necked guitar called the Sevena, or Sevener.

years.h: 88 Boadrum: 88 drummers, 88 minutes, the La Brea Tar Pits
years.p: At 8:08 pm on 8/8/08, Boredoms lead 88 drummers for 88 minutes at the La Brea Tar Pits in Los Angeles. A second 88 Boadrum in Brooklyn is conducted by [[Gang Gang Dance|83f1cb07-1745-48e6-8576-428604e67aa8]].
years.xp: Pitchfork's headline on the announcement was that Nike was bringing 88 Boadrum to LA and Brooklyn. Rolling Stone covered the band's taste for rhythm and numerology that August.

years.h: Super Roots 10
years.p: Another installment in Boredoms' long-running Super Roots EP series.

years.h: Boadrum 9: nine drummers at Terminal 5
years.p: At 9:09 pm on 9/9/09 at Terminal 5 in Manhattan, Yoshimi and Yojiro Tatekawa play with seven guests, among them [[Zach Hill|df6a1106-6caf-465b-bcfd-0b80d2b53516]] of [[Hella|1ecbc7e5-6e33-4062-997d-abc550dd63e6]] and Kid Millions of [[Oneida|33c5f321-37b5-4c8e-8eff-a8a6a5ac2e44]].

years.h: Two Boadrums at Matt Groening's ATP
years.p: Boredoms play two Boadrum sets at All Tomorrow's Parties, curated by Matt Groening at Butlins in Minehead, and tour London, Japan, Mexico and Melbourne.

years.h: Six drummers, a circle, and motion sensors in Tokyo
years.p: At ATP's I'll Be Your Mirror in Tokyo, six drummers circle Eye, who triggers drones by Shinji Masuko with motion sensors. Masuko becomes a full member.

years.h: 111 Boadrum at Byron Bay, 11:11 am
years.p: The last numbered Boadrum: 11 drummers and 100 cymbal players, 111 in all, at Byron Bay, Australia, at 11:11 am on 11/11/11.

years.h: Jeff Mangum's ATP: 14 guitarists and six drummers
years.p: Picked by [[Neutral Milk Hotel|a506f761-2c22-4b2f-8a94-bd748c2c8f75]]'s [[Jeff Mangum|6a7b9d5e-a863-4a90-a056-77942e9f43de]] for his All Tomorrow's Parties in Minehead, Boredoms play twice with 14 guitarists and six drummers.

years.h: A Boadrum at the Barbican with 88 cymbal players
years.p: Boredoms play London's Barbican as part of Doug Aitken's Station to Station: A 30-Day Happening, ringed by 88 percussionists all playing cymbals.
